question: What are the major degradation processes in high-voltage ternary cathode materials and how do they impact their performance?
answer: High-voltage operation of ternary cathode materials (TCMs) leads to several degradation processes, primarily affecting electrode/electrolyte interfacial stability. These processes include structural variations and exfoliation of the TCMs, parasitic reactions with the electrolyte, oxygen loss, and microcracking.  These ultimately cause irreversible structural collapse, loss of electronic contact, increased internal resistance, and reduced reversible capacity.

The purpose of the paper is to review the development and challenges of high-voltage ternary cathode materials (TCMs) for lithium-ion batteries (LIBs), particularly for next-generation long-range electric vehicles (EVs).
